transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/Time: 2027-06-09 15:00 UTC
- Duration: 48 min
- Attendees: Jordan Lee, Priya Nair, Miles Carter (Redwood) / Dr. Maya Singh, Liam O'Connor, Aisha Rahman, Hendrix Zhao (Centauri)

[00:00] Jordan: hey good afternoon everyone, thanks for joining. how's everybody doing?
[00:06] Dr. Maya Singh: good thanks, uh busy but, yeah excited to talk through the renewal and the eu pilot.
[00:12] Jordan: awesome, quick agenda — recap current usage, discuss capacity uplift options, eu vpc pilot, security docs, and next steps. sound ok?
[00:20] Liam: yep that's the list. i'd like to jump in on the playbook for burst/failover — we've had two spikes in april that impacted p99 latency.
[00:28] Priya: right, and we actually instrumented those spikes on our side, so we can show how continuous batching + kv prefix caching would help.
[00:36] Hendrix: before we get too deep, stan—standards: we'll need KMS integration, BYOK, and audit logs retained for 13 months at least. SOC2 attestation as well.
[00:45] Miles: totally, we can surface SOC2 and pen-test summaries. jordan will own getting the detailed artifacts over.
[00:50] Jordan: i'll put that in action items. quick question on timeline — procurement, where are you in terms of calendar?
[00:55] Aisha Rahman: we're aiming to close procurement by mid-july. procurement needs a redlined SOW and pricing by next week ideally.
[01:03] Jordan: ok noted — we'll prioritize that.
[01:08] Dr. Maya Singh: on capacity — our current retainer is 120k tokens/day average, but Q4 projections look like 3.5x. we want to add reserved capacity and a small dedicated pool for critical paths.
[01:20] Priya: when you say small dedicated — are you thinking dedicated GPUs pinned for inference, or reserved capacity on hosted with burst?
[01:26] Liam: ideally dedicated for the healthcare-critical calls (real-time triage), but cheaper hosted for batch workloads.
[01:32] Priya: makes sense. we usually recommend a hybrid: a dedicated pool for latency SLOs (p95/p99), plus hosted for the background. quantization/kv-cache profiles can keep costs down.
[01:43] Dr. Maya Singh: what are the latency numbers we can expect? our goal is p95 < 120ms for the triage flow at 8k qps.
[01:51] Priya: p95 under 120ms is ambitious at 8k qps, depends on sequence length. with a dedicated A100-ish cluster and optimized kernels we can approach that for short seqs, but long-context flows will increase it. we should run a targeted benchmark.
[02:06] Liam: can you simulate our worst-case token lengths? we have a lot of 1.5k token transcripts.
[02:12] Priya: yes, we can replay your traces — please share the traces and we'll run dedicated vs hosted.
[02:18] Jordan: action item — liam to provide traces and peak qps cadence.
[02:22] Aisha: procurement also wants clear failover — if dedicated goes down, how do we fail to hosted without dropping calls?
[02:29] Miles: we have a smart routing layer — automated fallback to a compatible model variant and region. there is a cold-start penalty but we can minimize impact with prefix caching and a warm standby.
[02:40] Hendrix: what's the network topology for the eu vpc pilot? we need private control plane and customer-managed networking.
[02:47] Priya: the pilot would be a VPC peering + private control plane; you'll manage the subnets and security groups. the data plane stays in your dedicated cluster in eu-central1.
[02:58] Hendrix: and KMS — we want HSM-backed keys. can you support external HSM?
[03:04] Miles: yes, we integrate with customer KMS/HSM and can offer BYOK flow; we'll share the integration guide.
[03:11] Jordan: i'll attach our KMS/HSM integration doc.
[03:14] Dr. Maya Singh: pricing — we need the math on reserved capacity vs overage. last renewal felt like there was some ambiguity on burst credits.
[03:23] Jordan: understood. we'll send a tiered pricing sheet — base retainer, dedicated pool surcharge, burst credits, and a cap option. we can add a clause for auto-burst to hosted at a known uplift.
[03:35] Aisha: and procurement needs the SOW with sample SLAs, on-call, and escalation matrix.
[03:41] Jordan: we can produce that by 2027-06-15.
[03:45] Liam: whats the expected prep window for the pilot? we need to align engineers and firewall changes.
[03:50] Priya: for a small eu VPC pilot (one cluster, private control plane), typical lead time is 2-3 weeks from kickoff; if you can provide infra IP allowlist and KMS contacts we can accelerate.
[04:01] Dr. Maya Singh: ok so kickoff week of 6/21 works for us.
[04:05] Hendrix: quick question on data residency — logs for model invocation, do they stay in the eu cluster?
[04:11] Miles: yes, for the private deployment pilot logs and telemetry can be retained in-region per the config, and audit logs can be routed to your SIEM via syslog/forwarder.
[04:20] Jordan: any competitors in the running?
[04:22] Dr. Maya Singh: we had an RFP, LambdaCloud and VertexOps responded; pricing competitive but security bar stronger with Redwood on certain items.
[04:31] Priya: cool. one more technical note — for your 1.5k token traces we recommend a KV cache policy and gpt-quant profile to drop memory without quality loss. we'll propose quant settings in the benchmark run.
[04:43] Liam: agreed, also can we get per-token cost estimates for a dedicated pool vs hosted at our seq distribution?
[04:49] Jordan: yes that's part of the pricing spreadsheet. we'll include per-token modeling and an example monthly TCO.
[04:55] Aisha: procurement will want a comparison table — committed retainer vs on-demand vs mixed.
[04:59] Jordan: we'll include that.
[05:02] Hendrix: on compliance artifacts — we need SOC2 + encryption at rest proof, and a statement about RBAC + SAML/SSO integration options.
[05:10] Miles: we support SAML SSO and fine-grained RBAC; i'll include a sample RBAC matrix. SOC2 report is available on request.
[05:18] Dr. Maya Singh: what about incident playbooks for model drift or quality regressions? we need regression alerts tied to prompt sets.
[05:25] Priya: Redwood Optimize includes quality monitoring, regressions alerts; we can wire your eval set to trigger alerts and auto-roll back to previous model version if regression detected.
[05:34] Liam: how fast is rollback? we need sub-10 minute remediation for triage flows.
[05:38] Priya: rollback is typically near-immediate for the control plane; full heat-up of caches might take a few minutes depending on traffic — we'll show an example in the pilot.
[05:47] Aisha: back to procurement — will legal need any special terms for data residency?
[05:52] Jordan: we'll add a data residency clause for the pilot SOW.
[05:56] Dr. Maya Singh: ok i'm broadly positive — the only blockers are KMS integration details, updated pricing, and a brief perf readout.
[06:04] Jordan: great. to recap next steps: jordan send pricing+SOW; priya run benchmarks; liam provide traces; hendrix send KMS contact and compliance asks; schedule pilot week of 6/21.
[06:18] Aisha: can we also get a runbook for the cutover and a rollback checklist?
[06:23] Miles: yes we'll prepare a runbook and share as part of the pilot artifacts.
[06:28] Dr. Maya Singh: excellent. one last minor note — network egress estimates, i'm going to need that for budgeting.
[06:34] Jordan: we'll model egress in the TCO sheet.
[06:38] Liam: thanks everyone.
[06:40] Jordan: thanks — we'll follow up in the tracker and i'll email the pricing + SOW.
[06:44] Dr. Maya Singh: thanks all. bye.
